body.input: The knockout stage is here! Eight teams, best-of-five, and the dream of lifting the Summoner’s Cup on the fourteenth of November in Brooklyn.
Yes, and if you missed the Swiss stage, you also missed Gen.G and Dplus KIA going three and oh, while G2 Esports packed their bags at one and three.
But Karmine Corp! First French team in the knockouts since Against All Authority in two thousand eleven!
They scraped through play-ins, then beat Anyone’s Legend, CTBC Flying Oyster, and Movistar KOI to finish three and two.
And now they face T1 on the sixth of November. The three-time defending champs.
Oh, brilliant. So either the fairy tale continues or reality hits like a Thresh hook.
And Gen.G take on LYON on the fourth of November! LYON’s first ever Worlds playoffs—this is their moment!
LYON did go three and two in Swiss, but Gen.G didn’t drop a game.
Ugh, facts. Fine. But Dplus KIA versus Bilibili Gaming on the fifth—that’s fire.
And Top Esports versus Invictus Gaming already happened on the third. No results yet, though.
Semifinals on the seventh and eighth, then Brooklyn. Five million dollar prize pool, a million to the winner.
So, Paul, who’s your dark horse? Or are you just here to cheer for everyone?
Karmine Corp. All the way.
Of course you are. Alright, we’ll leave it there.
